newsitem.title: UK: AIC says Cargill defaults again on Nov gas oil.
newsitem.headline: AIC says Cargill defaults again on Nov gas oil.

text.p: Trading house AIC, the main short on the November IPE gas oil contract, said on Tuesday Cargill had defaulted on its obligations in the second five-day window of the delivery period.

An AIC spokesman said by telephone that Cargill, the dominant long, had failed to lift 50 percent of the amount it was due to take in Amsterdam and 70 percent of the amount it was due to take in Antwerp, during the November 21-25 window.
"Cargill has defaulted again," the spokesman said.
A Cargill trader in Geneva declined to comment. A spokeswoman at Cargill's U.S. headquarters in Minneapolis could not immediately be reached for comment.
The AIC spokesman added: "Cargill has defaulted again and has short-lifed in the Amsterdam volume by as much as 50 percent or greater and in Antwerp by about 70 percent or greater."
"It's another default situation. It has to go the (International Petroleum) Exchange and the exchange will so deal with it. We will live by the rules of the exchange as we always have."

AIC last week said Cargill had failed to lift the required volume in the first five-day period of the November 16-30 delivery window. Cargill said on Thursday there had been some problems in the first five-day delivery period but it hoped to resolve these through IPE channels.

Cargill said earlier on Tuesday it was working with the IPE and all parties to the November IPE gas oil contract to resolve what it called continuing problems of delivery. It said it was confident that such issues would be resolved promptly through the IPE.

Discussing the alleged delivery problems, the AIC spokesman added without elaborating on Tuesday: "They (the IPE) will have to do some some sort of price backing clause and we'll have to take back our oil and dispense of it in a weak market, and obviously try to mitigate things."
IPE chief executive Lynton Jones said last week the exchange was closely monitoring the delivery of the November gas oil futures contract to ensure performance by the dominant short and long.
